# Bench sink r1: mount comparison (generated by scripts/compare_mounts.py; do not edit)

## A. Common sink + selected shims (revision 2; bench_thermal.py / bench_tolerance.py, bound case)

- 17.5 A: sink 72.8 C, Tj 87.1 C; 22 A: sink 85.7 C (fan), Tj 111.6 C. One NTC and one TCO see all five devices' heat.
- Hand work: gauge 8 gaps, run shim_select.py, cut and grease up to 3 layers x 4, float and lock the sink.

## B. One sink per device

Width window for a per-device sink: >= 14.15 mm (cover E1 max) and <= 17.50 mm (18 mm pitch at Q5/Q6 and Q3/Q2, 0.5 mm fitting gap). Strip at a 45 N clip on the small tab: 1.489 C/W.

- **No catalogue TO-247 sink in the read fits the pitch** (narrowest 19.4 mm). The ones that would hold 22 A are 35-42 mm wide. A per-device bench would need custom 17 mm sinks (e.g. slices of an extrusion) and custom clips.
- A FET sink that carried the TCO would need R_SA <= 6.03 C/W at 22 A (8.30 W). BR1 alone dissipates 25.52 W: its own sink needs R_SA <= 1.96 C/W to stay <= 80 C, so BR1's sink is the hottest and the TCO/NTC would sit there, **seeing none of the FETs**. A fan-shadowed or badly clipped FET sink then overheats with no sink-sensed trip; the common sink's NTC sees every device's heat (not a bad interface, in either design).
- A sink that hangs on its device loads the soldered leads: elastic moment at the weakest lead corner 27.8 N mm, so at a 34 mm lever (EST centre of mass) the sink must weigh <= 83 g (before any fan or harness pull), or sit on its own support - which brings back a positioning fit per device.
- Insulation: each tab still needs >= 4 mm of pad beyond its metal edge on every side; at the 18 mm pitch the pads overlap, so the per-device design still needs one continuous strip across the separate sinks, plus five PE bonds (one per sink).

## C. Common sink + thick soft gap pad (GAP PAD 5000S35, no shims, no spring clamp)

Usable thickness window = 10-30 % strain (the data range [HNK] p.28). Spread to absorb: R 0.270-0.570 mm, U 1.800-2.100 mm, plus up to 0.179 mm of lean wedge per device.
